correctness.rationale: Perfect measurement resets exactly the observed coordinate error. The symmetric two-state Markov sensor has stationary consecutive run K with P(K=k)=eps r^(k-1), and the other coordinate error has conditional normal variance C(B^k-1), independent of K. This yields exact covariance tail, moments, mean q/(1-rB), and a Gaussian scale mixture for |E|. Rescaling z²/C=B^(N+theta), geometric upper-j tail and super-Gaussian lower-j tail justify uniform phase-dependent convergence; Mellin transform gives Fourier coefficients proportional 2^s Γ(s+1/2)/s, nonzero for all harmonics. Strict convexity yields the stated unique switching-price optimum in the symmetric Markov family. Independently evaluated 9 phase-tail asymptotic cases, first complex Fourier harmonic and switching-cost grid.
residual_risks: Stationarity of measurement errors (not unstable latent state); exact noiseless observations, two identical modes, ε>0, no general adaptive-policy optimum.

value.rationale: It isolates the exact Gaussian rather than covariance tail in a natural two-sensor scheduling model, proves the genuinely nonconstant lattice modulation at every harmonic, identifies sharp moment bounds and gives an explicit price-dependent sensor switching policy within a well-stated class. The precise arithmetic amplitude resolves a coefficient question left open/difficult in the relevant general theory and is a useful tail-quantile diagnostic.
residual_risks: Scope does not extend to general Kalman filters or unconstrained adaptive sensor scheduling.
